spec.title: Catalogue: the seams of upstream a delta can use

status.comment: edition 1.0.0; example locations were verified on upstream tag 1.135.0 on 2026-09-07 and are cited as paths and line numbers only, never as code

p.SEAM-CATALOGUE-IS-A-MENU-NOT-AN-INSTANCE: This catalogue lists the ways upstream itself lets a distribution add or change behaviour, ranked by how far upstream sanctions them. It is a **menu**: a product picks from it the seams its delta actually leans on and records those, dated to its pin, as its own seam map (`MI-SEAM-MAP-REQUIRED`); the map is an instance that lives in the product and names the product's interventions, this catalogue names neither.

p.SEAM-CATALOGUE-EXAMPLES-ARE-LOCATIONS-NO: Every example here is a path and, where useful, a line number on one upstream tag. The catalogue quotes no upstream code: a location is a fact about where a seam sits, code would be a copy of someone else's work. A location that moved on a newer tag is a reason to re-validate the row, not the seam.

p.SEAM-CATALOGUE-ORDER: Tiers run from the most sanctioned to the least: a change upstream itself accepts, data upstream reads, upstream's own extension mechanisms, a graft into an entry, a hook in a body, a type, the build and hygiene registries, and finally the internals of an upstream module. A new intervention looks for the highest tier that expresses it (`MI-SEAM-MAP-IS-RANKED`).

p.SEAM-UPSTREAM-PR: A pull request upstream that parameterises a string or a behaviour by the product configuration costs nothing after it merges; upstream already parameterises many user-facing strings by the product's short and long names, so the convention exists. Use it for the few visible strings the product wants clean at the source, not for hundreds.

tier-1.title: Tier 1 — data upstream reads, no code

facts.SEAM-PRODUCT-JSON: `product.json` is the widest seam: its type (`src/vs/base/common/product.ts`) declares well over a hundred fields — identity and names, Windows installer identifiers, URLs and endpoints, the extension gallery and recommendations, telemetry and experiments, built-in extensions and API proposals, onboarding themes and keymaps, licence and server fields — and the open-source build uses only a few dozen of them. Extra keys survive to the product service in every process, so a product may add its own bag of keys and type it by augmentation (tier 5). Codkit layer: config-overlay with `expectUpstream`.
facts.SEAM-PRODUCT-OVERRIDES: `product.overrides.json` is merged only in development builds (`src/bootstrap-meta.ts`, the web client server), shallowly, and is excluded from a shipped build; it is the development channel of the overlay, never a delivery seam.
facts.SEAM-BUILD-TEMPLATES: Packaging reads `product.json` at build time: Linux desktop files, appdata, rpm and deb metadata and shell completions (`build/gulpfile.vscode.linux.ts`), the Windows installer defines (`build/gulpfile.vscode.win32.ts`, template `build/win32/code.iss`), the macOS bundle through the packaging library (`build/lib/electron.ts`), the server scripts (`build/gulpfile.reh.ts`), and the Rust CLI's constants (`cli/build.rs`, with defaults in `cli/src/constants.rs`). One overlay reaches all of them.
facts.SEAM-RESOURCES: Application icons, installer artwork, the server favicon and the editor watermarks are files at fixed upstream paths, referenced from CSS backgrounds and image tags that no icon theme reaches (for example the title-bar icon in `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/media/titlebarpart.css`). Codkit layer: resource-file with a mandatory guard.
facts.SEAM-PRODUCT-ICON-THEME: Every icon drawn through the icon registry (`src/vs/platform/theme/common/iconRegistry.ts`) can be replaced by a product icon theme contributed by an extension; the style sheet is generated for registry icons only (`src/vs/platform/theme/browser/iconsStyleSheet.ts`), so CSS-background images stay with the resource seam. The default icon theme and the default colour themes are setting defaults in code (`src/vs/workbench/services/themes/common/workbenchThemeService.ts`), not `product.json` keys; the channel to change them is the `configurationDefaults` extension point or a registered default configuration.
facts.SEAM-BUILT-IN-EXTENSION: A folder under `extensions/` with a valid `package.json` is packaged by a glob (`build/lib/extensions.ts`), so a declarative extension — themes, grammars, snippets, a language pack — needs no build change; an extension with TypeScript needs two entries in the build's own lists (`build/gulpfile.extensions.ts`, `build/npm/dirs.ts`), which belong to the constant graft set. The extension API is the most sanctioned seam after `product.json`; upstream ships its own default themes this way (`extensions/theme-defaults`).
facts.SEAM-LANGUAGE-PACK: A language pack is a built-in extension contributing `localizations`; its translation file maps module paths to keys to strings (`build/lib/i18n.ts`), and the shared process registers installed packs at startup (`src/vs/code/electron-utility/sharedProcess/contrib/localizationsUpdater.ts`). Upstream forces English in development builds and for `en*` locales (`src/vs/base/node/nls.ts`), so a pack is proven in a built product, never in the development tree.
facts.SEAM-EXTENSION-POINTS: Upstream registers several dozen extension points; the ones a distribution reaches for are `localizations`, `walkthroughs`, `themes`, `iconThemes`, `productIconThemes`, `configurationDefaults`, `commands`, `menus`, `keybindings`, `viewsWelcome`, `views` and `viewsContainers`. There is no extension point for the welcome page's start entries: those are core data.

tier-2.title: Tier 2 — upstream's own mechanisms for extending the core

facts.SEAM-DI: Services are registered with `registerSingleton` into an append-only list (`src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/extensions.ts`); the renderer (`src/vs/workbench/browser/workbench.ts`) and the extension host copy that list into a collection where the last registration of an id wins. The main process, the shared process, the server and the CLI assemble their services explicitly and never read the list, and the product service is set explicitly in every process: a service override reaches the renderer and the extension host only (`MI-SERVICE-OVERRIDE-REACH`).
facts.SEAM-WORKBENCH-CONTRIBUTION: `registerWorkbenchContribution2` (`src/vs/workbench/common/contributions.ts`) creates a class at a lifecycle phase — blocking startup, blocking restore, after restore, eventually — or lazily, or when an editor of a type opens; a duplicate id is logged, not overridden; a late registration is instantiated at once. Hundreds of upstream features are wired this way, and so is own code.
facts.SEAM-REGISTRIES: About thirty registries hang off `Registry.add` (`src/vs/platform/registry/common/platform.ts`, ids unique by assertion): configuration, views and view containers, editor panes, quick access, output channels, JSON schemas, colours, icons, theming participants, actions, commands, menus and keybindings. Own code registers into them from its composition root exactly as an upstream contribution does.
facts.SEAM-DEFAULT-OVERRIDES: `registerDefaultConfigurations` (`src/vs/platform/configuration/common/configurationRegistry.ts`) restates the default of any upstream setting without declaring it, and the colour registry's `updateDefaultColor` restates a colour; upstream's own second product does both from its entry. Upstream calls the first a last resort because tooling cannot see it: a hide recorded with a guard, not a habit.
facts.SEAM-CONTEXT-KEYS: Every setting is a context key (`config.<id>`) usable in `when` clauses; own code publishes its own keys through the context key service, and a feature flag published as `<id>.enabled` moves menus, commands and views without code.
facts.SEAM-NEW-EXTENSION-POINT: Own code may define a new extension point (`src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/common/extensionsRegistry.ts`): the registry is a module singleton that throws only on a duplicate name and registers the contribution schema itself.
facts.SEAM-SURFACE-REGISTRY: Upstream's own second product keeps a service for full-surface contributed views that replace its centre: a registry whose registration is a disposable, the active view as an observable, `show`/`hide`, and a restore key in storage; the view itself is an abstract class with an observable title, `render(container)`, `layout(width, height)` and `focus()`. A product that hosts its own surfaces gives them that shape (`MI-SAME-SHAPE-AS-UPSTREAMS-PARALLEL-SYSTEM`).
facts.SEAM-LATE-REGISTRATION-IS-SANCTIONED: Upstream's own second product replaces the editor-groups service and the pane-composite host by a late `registerSingleton` of its own classes, and reaches the main editor part through a `protected` factory method meant for subclassing. Both are therefore sanctioned seams for a product, with the same limits as `MI-SERVICE-OVERRIDE-REACH`.
facts.SEAM-PART-OPTIONS: Options of an upstream part are imposed through its disposable option API (the editor part's `enforcePartOptions`), which wins over the user's setting for as long as the disposable lives — the form for a product-fixed presentation.
facts.SEAM-HIDE-WHAT-CAN-BE-HIDDEN: View containers and views can be deregistered (`src/vs/workbench/common/views.ts`), output channels removed, icons deregistered, configurations and default configurations deregistered — from any core module, with a guard. Menu items, commands and core walkthroughs cannot: the menu registry has no removal, registering a second action with the same id throws, and re-registering a walkthrough id is refused; hiding those is a `when` clause the item already honours, or a patch with a named reason.

tier-3.title: Tier 3 — a graft into the entry of a process

facts.SEAM-ENTRY-PER-PROCESS: Each process has one entry: the renderer's shared list of contributions (`src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts`, imported by both the desktop and the web entry, so one graft there reaches both), the desktop and web entries, the main process (`src/vs/code/electron-main/main.ts`, reached from the bootstrap by a dynamic import), the shared process (`src/vs/code/electron-utility/sharedProcess/sharedProcessMain.ts`), the server (`src/vs/server/node/server.main.ts` and its service assembly), the extension host (`src/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.ts`), and the bootstrap files at `src/*.ts`, which have no channel at all. One graft per process, none for bootstrap (`MI-ONE-GRAFT-PER-PROCESS`, `MI-BOOTSTRAP-HAS-NO-CHANNEL`).
facts.SEAM-GRAFT-IS-RELATIVE: A graft import must be relative: upstream's lint rejects an absolute `vs/...` specifier inside `src/vs`. Bundling follows imports transitively with no directory list (`build/lib/optimize.ts`), so a grafted module ships without a build change; a separate bundle of its own needs an entry in both entry-point lists (`build/buildfile.ts`, `build/next/index.ts`).
facts.SEAM-UPSTREAM-PARALLEL-SYSTEM: Upstream's own second product (`src/vs/sessions/`) is the precedent for a parallel system: its own entry files, `services/`, `contrib/`, a layers document, and import-pattern targets of its own in `eslint.config.js`; the workbench never imports it. A product's own layer is shaped the same way (`MI-UPSTREAM-HAS-A-PARALLEL-SYSTEM`).

tier-4.title: Tier 4 — a hook in an upstream body

facts.SEAM-HOOK-IS-A-GRAFT: Where no seam exists, a patch places a hook at a composition point: one import or one call into own code, nothing more (`MI-PATCH-IS-A-GRAFT`). What breaks when the pin moves is the context around the marker; what catches it is the three-way merge at `sync` and a contract test on the behaviour.
facts.SEAM-STRING-FUNNELS: Every user-facing string of the core passes one function (`_format` in `src/vs/nls.ts`) on both its paths — the English default in development and the bundled lookup in a build — so one hook there brands every core string in every language after the language pack has spoken; manifest strings of extensions pass `localizeManifest` (`src/vs/platform/extensionManagement/common/extensionNls.ts`), and strings of extension code pass the extension host's localization service (`src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLocalizationService.ts`). The Rust CLI has no funnel; its names come from the build constants. Three hooks and one own rule table replace hundreds of string patches; a snapshot of the affected keys is the guard.
facts.SEAM-DOCKING-A-PART: A part can be shown inside another part: upstream's own second product moves the auxiliary bar's element into the editor part's content area and lays it out by hand. The moved part keeps asking the layout service whether it is visible, and the layout hides the active composite when it hides the node — so a product docks through a layout adapter given to the part in a child instantiation scope and a replaced pane-composite host, never through a patch of the layout.
facts.SEAM-BOOTSTRAP-HOOK: Bootstrap has no dependency injection: a behaviour that must exist before the workbench (the default locale, for instance, in `src/main.ts`) is a hook that calls an own function; the logic and its unit test live in own code.

p.SEAM-TYPE-AUGMENTATION: An own `.d.ts` that augments an exported upstream interface through a relative module specifier compiles under upstream's own compiler settings, and `src/tsconfig.json` already includes every `.ts` under `src/vs`, so a product's extra `product.json` keys get their type without a patch of `src/vs/base/common/product.ts`. Upstream does not use the technique itself; it is not forbidden either. The guard is the compiler.

tier-6.title: Tier 6 — build and hygiene registries (the constant graft set)

facts.SEAM-IMPORT-PATTERNS: `local/code-import-patterns` in `eslint.config.js` has no catch-all target: a file under a new directory gets a "missing definition" warning that fails the lint, and a warning is a failure. The own directory needs a block of targets shaped like upstream's own top-level layer; that block is the first member of the constant graft set (`MI-GRAFT-SET-CONTENTS`).
facts.SEAM-LAYERING: `local/code-layering` works by folder name anywhere under the tree — `common`, `node`, `browser`, `electron-browser`, `electron-utility`, `electron-main` — so own code that keeps upstream's folder names is checked automatically and needs no entry.
facts.SEAM-HEADER-HYGIENE: The `header/header` rule applies to every linted file with no exemption list, and the hygiene task compares the first four lines of a source file with upstream's header byte for byte (`build/hygiene.ts`); the filters (`build/filters.ts`) exclude by extension, and know neither `.toml`, `.csv` nor `.license`. The exemption for own files is one data line in the copyright filter (`MI-HEADER-EXEMPTION-FORM`); files of unknown extension get an exclusion line beside it.
facts.SEAM-RESOURCE-LISTS: Non-JavaScript assets reach a packaged build only through allow-lists, in both bundling pipelines (`build/gulpfile.vscode.ts`, `build/next/index.ts`); the development tree hides an omission because it reads files from disk. One glob per pipeline for the own directory's assets, verified by the packaged-build proof.
facts.SEAM-NLS-EXTRACTION: Localizable strings are extracted from every compiled module with no allow-list (`build/lib/nls.ts`), but the XLF export throws on a module prefix it does not know (`build/lib/i18n.ts`): a branch there belongs to the graft set only when the product exports XLF.
facts.SEAM-MINIFIER-ASCII: The minifier rejects a non-ASCII character in its output (`build/lib/optimize.ts`): own code carries no non-ASCII literals; strings go through `nls`, translations through a pack.
facts.SEAM-TESTS-AND-TSCONFIG: `src/tsconfig.json` includes every `.ts` under `src/vs`, and the unit-test runners find `test/**/*.test.js` under the own directory by glob; neither needs an entry.

tier-7.title: Tier 7 — the internals of an upstream module

p.SEAM-INTERNALS-ARE-PATCH-EQUIVALENT: Mutating an exported array or object of an upstream module, depending on the load order of modules, or reading another component's storage keys (which upstream's own guidelines forbid) is a patch equivalent wherever the file lives (`MI-INTERNALS-ARE-PATCH-EQUIVALENT`): it needs a contract test, it never throws while a module is evaluated, and the seam map names it as such.

facts.NEVER-TREAT-THE-CATALOGUE-AS-THE-MAP: Never cite this catalogue as the product's seam map: the map is the product's own instance, dated to its pin, naming its interventions.
facts.NEVER-QUOTE-UPSTREAM-CODE-IN-A-STANDARD: Never paste upstream code into a standard or into this catalogue — cite a path and a line.
